correctness.rationale: IID atomless endpoints give a uniform perfect matching of ranks. An interval is minimal exactly when it opens before the first right endpoint, so M_n≥k means no internal match in the first k ranks. Reflection gives the analogous last-l ranks event. Conditional on j initial openings, the next endpoint is new with probability (2n−2j)/(2n−j). For the joint event the rank blocks A,B are disjoint; choose and biject h endpoints of each to make the A–B pairs, assign the remaining k+l−2h labeled vertices injectively into the middle c, and pair the remaining 2z middle ranks. The product is exactly k!l!c!/[h!(k−h)!(l−h)!2^z z!], with the stated bounds from z≥0 and h≤min(k,l). This includes k or l zero and n=1; mixed finite differences give the masses. For uniform endpoints, the minimum right endpoint T and reflected maximum left endpoint W exclude disjoint squares of endpoint space for thresholds a+b≤1, giving (1−a²−b²)^n and the joint independent limit for sqrt(n)(T,W). Conditional on the winning interval and T=t, the other endpoint pairs are independent truncated to R>t, with P(L≤t | R>t)=2t/(1+t); this distribution does not depend on the winning index. Thus the scaled difference between the counts and 2sqrt(n)(T,W) goes to zero in L²: conditional variance is O(n E T)=O(sqrt(n)), and the squared bias is O(1) by E T^4=O(n^−2). Reflection handles W. The product bound exp(−k(k−1)/(4n)) gives uniform fourth moments and uniform integrability of scaled squares and products. Integrating the limiting tail gives mean sqrt(pi) and second moment 4, hence the stated variance and zero limiting correlation. The checker was read, not run; the argument proves all n.
residual_risks: Requires IID atomless endpoints and precedence order; not a claim about finite-n independence or unscaled covariance.
